thread:
ryan: quick heads-up — noticed p99 jump during a recent burst test when autoscale added nodes. baseline looks fine but tails spike ~2.5x for ~30s after scale-up. anyone seen this pattern?

maya: saw similar on canary yesterday. kernel selector falls back to generic matmul on new instances while JIT/kernels warm. fallback latency + kv cold misses amplify tail.

liam: +1. also observed that microbatch sizes inflate during scale events because our per-worker queue gets drained unevenly. some requests go to newly spun GPUs with empty KV cache => full context regen.

ryan: attaching profiler snippets from last run (copied). the hot path is the attention kernel fallback and the kv cache miss loop.

-- profiler snippet --
flame: runtime.attn_fp16_generic  42%
runtime.attn_opt_kernel      12%
kv_cache.lookup_miss         18%
kv_cache.populate           10%
runtime.dispatch_overhead    6%
-- end snippet --

aanya: interesting — fallback to attn_fp16_generic explains the per-token slowdown. If kernel selector uses sequence-length heuristics, maybe warmup ordering causes mismatch. New nodes see short sequences then long ones -> kernel mispick.

maya: proposal: when a node first joins during burst, force it into a 'preheat' path: run a few synthetic microbatches that exercise long-seq kernels and populate KV prefixes. cheap warmup container that executes: 

```
# warmup worker script (pseudo)
for i in range(8):
  send_inference(prompt_stub_long_seq, batch_size=1, use_kv=true)
```

this should prime kernels and KV without affecting live quotas.

liam: we can also bias microbatch assignment: prefer routing small concurrent requests to warmed nodes and funnel large ones to nodes that finished warmup. That reduces kernel-selector confusion.

ryan: curious about tradeoffs — how does forced warmup affect throughput and cost? we don't want to waste too many cycles. maybe ephemeral burst-capacity budget can pay for 1s warmup per GPU.

maya: ran a sim with 1s warmup per GPU + targeted microbatching heuristic (cap microbatch at 8 for first 10s). result: p95 unchanged, p99 down from 2.5x spike to ~1.1x. tail duration dropped from ~30s to ~7s in our sim.

liam: any perf regression flags we should add? i noticed after last release kernel-selector got a change to avoid calling CUDA kernel version X for seq<64. that rule might be too aggressive when queues are shallow.

ryan: can you paste the selector logic snippet? maybe make it consider recent selection success metrics (last N runs) in addition to static seq length.

liam: sure — current pseudocode:

```
if seq_len < 64:
  use_kernel('fast_short')
elif seq_len < 512:
  use_kernel('balanced')
else:
  use_kernel('long_opt')
```

we could change to:

```
if recent_fail_rate('fast_short') > 0.1:
  escalate_to('balanced')
else:
  keep_heuristic_based
```

maya: +1 to going metric-driven. also add kv_cache.miss_rate into selector decision. if miss_rate > 0.2 prefer kernels that tolerate cold-KV.

aanya: operational note: autoscaler emits scale events to #deploy-bot during burst. we can subscribe our runtime warmup hook to those events to avoid custom orchestration. ops-bot should have a tag for new_node_ids.

ops-bot: scale event: added 16 gpus (pool: burst-64) at 2026-03-10T14:22:13Z — node_ids: [i-0a1b2c, i-0a1b2d, ...]

ryan: perfect — i'll prototype a warmup lambda that listens and runs warmup script. also will add a short-lived microbatch cap for the first 15s post-scale.

liam: for experiments, let's capture per-node kernel-choice histograms + kv_miss_rate and correlate with tail-latency. that will let us A/B rule changes without guessing.

maya: logging plan: emit metrics: kernel_choice{node,model,seq_bucket}, kv_miss{node}, warmup_done{node}. dashboard for p95/p99 by node_age.

aanya: i'll add a small eval to Redwood Optimize to simulate cold-kv bursts and produce recommendations (warmup length, microbatch caps) per model family.

ryan: timeline: i'll push a PoC warmup hook + microbatch cap to canary tomorrow. if results match sim, we'll roll to prod for burst pools.

maya: thanks. small follow-up: we should also consider backoff for request routing to new nodes for the first N seconds to avoid concentration. simple circuit-breaker.

ryan: agreed. i'll add routing backoff. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
